title: Describing a mood presentation: mastery check

items.prompt: D. is 45 and works as a school caretaker. This is everything the appointment produced. D. says: "I've not been right since the new year. Can't be bothered with anything." D. says: "I'm in bed by nine and I still can't get up. Ten, eleven hours." A note from D.'s line manager, dated last month, records four late arrivals in six weeks. Observed across the appointment: D. spoke at normal rate and volume, and cried while describing the job. D. was not asked about weight, about appetite, or about any past period of raised activity. Write four elements covering mood and interest, sleep, function, and observed expression. Each element must state what changed, its time course, and its source. Then write the line or lines that record what is missing.

answer.correct: Mood and interest: lowered mood with loss of interest, since around the new year, continuous by D.'s account, D.'s report. Sleep: sleeping about ten to eleven hours with difficulty rising, in bed by about 21:00, onset not established, D.'s report; the direction is increased sleep. Function: four late arrivals in six weeks up to last month, line manager's record, which is another person's record and the only counted item here. Observed expression: tearful while describing the job; speech at normal rate and volume across the appointment; observed. Gaps: weight and appetite were not asked about, and no question was put about any past period of raised activity, so neither is an established negative.
answer.summary: Four elements, each with a change, a period, and a source, plus two recorded gaps.
answer.reasoning: Award one point for all four elements carrying a source that is one of self-report, another person's report, or observation, with the line manager's note correctly identified as another person's record. Award one point for the time courses, including writing that the sleep onset was not established instead of borrowing the new year from the mood element. Award one point for the two gaps written as gaps, and for the sleep element carrying its direction, which is increased sleep and the opposite of the case worked in the lesson. A response that writes 'sleep disturbance' without a direction does not earn the third point, because that line cannot be compared with anything at a later appointment. On a retry, use a different set: a person whose partner reports three months of early waking, who reports sleeping normally, whose employer's record shows no absence, and who was asked about unusual experiences and described none.
acceptableResponses: Any response giving four elements each with a change, a period, and one of the three sources, marking the sleep onset as not established, giving the sleep change a direction, and recording the unasked questions as gaps rather than as absences.
commonErrors: Borrowing the new year onset from the mood element onto the sleep element
Writing 'sleep disturbance' or 'poor sleep' without saying that D. is sleeping more
Recording the unasked questions as negatives, or leaving them out entirely
Treating the line manager's note as D.'s report, or as an observation of the assessor

items.prompt: A. is 38, and A.'s partner made the appointment. The partner says A. has been "flat and snappy" since about January and has stopped going to five-a-side football. A. says the sleep is "the same as always, six hours" and that work is unaffected. A. was tearful twice during the appointment and answered at normal speed. A. was asked about unusual experiences and beliefs and described none. Nobody asked about past periods of raised activity, about appetite, or about thoughts of death. For each of the nine kinds of change this lesson covers, say whether it is present, established as absent, or unaddressed by the record, and give the source wherever there is one. Then name the two questions you would ask first and say why those two.

answer.correct: Depressive: present since about January on the partner's report; A. has not described low mood directly, and the record keeps both accounts. Irritable: present since about January on the partner's report, unconfirmed by A. Elevated: unaddressed, never asked. Mixed: cannot be stated, because it depends on the elevated question that has not been put. Psychotic: established as absent, asked and denied. Cognitive: unaddressed. Sleep: A. reports about six hours and no change; the partner has not been asked, so this rests on one account. Energy: unaddressed; stopping five-a-side is suggestive and is a functional item, not an energy finding. Functional: stopped five-a-side since about January on the partner's report, and work unaffected on A.'s report. Observed: tearful twice, normal response speed, across one appointment. Ask first about any past period of raised activity, because it is the only unasked question that could change the shape of the whole picture and because the mixed question depends on it; and about thoughts of death, because it is unaddressed and because people do not usually raise it unprompted.
answer.summary: Three present on the partner's report, one established negative, four unaddressed, one self-reported as unchanged, and two priority questions with reasons.
answer.reasoning: Award one point for separating the unaddressed elements from the single established negative, which requires noticing that only the psychotic element was asked and answered. Award one point for correct sourcing throughout, including keeping the partner's account of low mood and A.'s silence on it side by side without resolving them, and for not converting the football into an energy finding. Award one point for the two priority questions with reasons that turn on what the answer could change, rather than on completeness. A response that lists all four unaddressed elements as absent does not earn the first point. On a retry, use a case where the person reports the low mood and the informant disagrees, and where cognitive change is the only element that was asked about.
acceptableResponses: Any response that separates unaddressed from established-absent, sources every populated element, refuses to state the mixed element until the elevated question is asked, and justifies two priority questions by what their answers could change.
commonErrors: Recording the four unasked elements as absent
Resolving the disagreement between A. and the partner instead of recording both
Reading 'stopped five-a-side' as an energy finding rather than a functional one
Choosing the two priority questions for completeness rather than for what an answer would change

items.prompt: A person tells you: "About four years ago I had a fortnight where I barely slept, started three jobs round the house and finished none of them, and my sister said I was talking nonsense at her down the phone at two in the morning. I felt great. I never saw anyone about it." Write the line that belongs in the record. Then write what a clinician reading your line in a year's time can do that they could not do if the line read "history of a hypomanic episode four years ago".

answer.correct: Reports a period of about two weeks roughly four years ago with markedly reduced sleep, several household projects started and not completed, and speech that a sister described at the time as talking nonsense during a call at two in the morning. Describes feeling great during it. Never assessed by any clinician. Source: the person's retrospective account, with the sister's remark reported second-hand within it. A clinician reading that in a year can seek the sister as an informant, ask what she noticed and over how many days, and compare any new period of raised activity against a described baseline. The shorter version supports none of that, because it asserts an assessment nobody made and hides both the source and the content, so the next reader has nothing to check and no reason to check it.
answer.summary: A dated, sourced, contentful line, plus the three things it makes possible that a diagnostic label removes.
answer.reasoning: Award one point for the line carrying duration, dating, and specific content instead of a category. Award one point for the source being written as a retrospective self-report that was never assessed, with the sister's comment identified as second-hand inside that account rather than as an informant's report. Award one point for naming at least two concrete things a later reader can do, at least one of which is seeking the informant or establishing the duration more exactly. A response that writes the line well and then justifies it only by saying that it is more accurate does not earn the third point, because the value of the longer line is what it makes possible later. On a retry, do the same for a person who reports 'three or four days of not needing sleep' during a bereavement two years ago, where the dating is vaguer and one further source exists.
acceptableResponses: Any response whose recorded line gives duration, approximate date, described content, and the retrospective self-report source, and which names at least two later actions the line supports.
commonErrors: Writing a classification such as hypomania, mania, or a bipolar-spectrum label into the record line
Treating the sister's remark as an informant's report rather than as second-hand content inside the person's own account
Dropping the person's own framing of the period, which is itself information
Recording that the period was never assessed but then writing the rest of the line as established fact

items.prompt: A person is seen again three months after a first appointment. Which line from the first appointment supports a statement about whether that element has changed?

options.text: Waking at about 05:00 and not returning to sleep, five or six nights a week, since March, on the person's own account.
Limited insight into the extent of the difficulties.

answer.summary: Only the sleep line carries a direction, a rate, a start date, and a source, so it can be set against the same measurement three months later.
answer.reasoning: The sleep line names what changed, how often, since when, and who says so, which is what makes a later comparison possible on like terms. 'Appetite reduced' has no rate, no date, and no source. 'Marked fatigue, longstanding' has an intensity word doing the work of a time course, and longstanding gives no start point. 'Limited insight' is an inference and not a finding at all, so a change in it would be a change in the assessor's judgement. Feedback for a wrong choice: reread the four time-course questions, and check each option for a direction and a start date before checking anything else.
commonErrors: Choosing the fatigue line because 'longstanding' looks like a time course
Choosing the insight line because it sounds like a clinical judgement worth tracking
Choosing the appetite line because reduced names a direction, without noticing the missing rate, date, and source

rubrics.title: Elements with change, period, and source

criteria.description: All four elements carry one of the three sources, and the line manager's note is identified as another person's record.
Time courses are given where established and marked as not established where they are not, without borrowing a date from another element.
The sleep change carries its direction, and the unasked questions are recorded as gaps rather than as negatives or silence.

rubrics.title: Present, established absent, or unaddressed across the nine

criteria.description: Unaddressed elements are separated from the single established negative, and silence is never reported as absence.
Every populated element carries its source, the two accounts of the low mood are kept side by side, and the functional item is not converted into an energy finding.
Two priority questions are chosen and justified by what their answers could change, including the dependency of the mixed element on the elevated question.

rubrics.title: A remembered period held at the strength of its source

criteria.description: The recorded line carries duration, approximate dating, and specific described content instead of a category.
The source is written as a retrospective self-report never assessed, with second-hand content inside it identified as such.
At least two concrete later actions are named that the line supports and a diagnostic label would prevent.

rubrics.title: Recognising a line that can be compared

criteria.description: Selects the line carrying direction, rate, start date, and source.
